attributions.reason: The native submit box and original PNG place the approved side strip entirely inside the disabled component button, away from text and host background. Frozen sampling recomputes a stable solid wrong fill (light #CFCDC5; dark #33474C), and the originals visibly show the whole disabled fill dimmed. The production code chooses the approved disabled palette but applies native .disabled with PlainButtonStyle, whose rendering changes it; the component owns final opaque fill under policy. This supports a product rendering failure, not sampling of a host-owned canvas. Exact platform style mechanism is an inference; measured mismatch remains authoritative.

Caller replacement is demonstrated in the same native instance with fixture index 1, new input hash, successful caller_fixture_update and no business callback. The original changed notice is visible, but native/current summary reads No work selected and b is visibly unselected. Actual delivered fixtures seed available b; the compiled bridge only decodes and forwards that model. The component failed to restore incoming selection on revision change. The precise SwiftUI closure/state mechanism is not established; product state failure is supported independently of that mechanism.

After the successfully advancing same-instance caller update, raw native submit enablement is false and the original button is visibly disabled. Delivered fixture 1 seeds available b, which should make the primary action enabled. New notice and correct input binding establish delivery. This is downstream of the component dropping its incoming b selection, not missing native activation or a stale-input screenshot.

The fully visible component button is rendered in the same dimmed disabled fill as baseline, whereas the authoritative new input seeds available b and requires an enabled action. This follows the component selection-replacement failure, with disabled styling also changing its final rendered palette. Original strip is internal solid fill, so observation suitability does not explain this F.
